sentences.text: Shri Shobhag Mal Porwal - Advocate for the applicant.
Shri Nilesh Dave - Advocate for the respondent No.1/accu
Shri Madhusudan Yadav - G.A. for respondent No.2/State.

Order 
1] They are heard and perused the documents.

2] This is an application filed under Section 439 (2) of Cr.P.C./483(3) of B.N.S.S. for cancellation of bail of respondent No.1/accused Bhaarat @ Bharat Bawari, who has been granted bail by this Court in M.Cr.C. No.22788 of 2024 dated 12.07.2024 in connection with Crime No.152 of 2023 registered at Police Station Malhargarh, District Mandsaur under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n) of IPC and Sections 5(l)/6, 5(J)
(ii)(l)/6 of POCSO Act for the offence of rape.

3] Counsel for the applicant has submitted that in the aforesaid order this Court has clearly opined that if the respondent No.1 is found to be involved in any other offence after being released on bail,
this order shall stand cancelled without further reference.

Counsel has submitted that subsequent to his release, the respondent No.1 has again committed another offence at Crime No.197 of 2024 at Police Station Pipliyamandi, District Mandsaur under the same provision, and he has eloped with the prosecutrix, the daughter of the present applicant, and thus, his order of bail deserves to be recalled.

NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:29311 2 MCRC-39301-2024 4] Counsel for the respondent No.1 has opposed the prayer, and it is submitted that in the subsequent case, the prosecutrix has already been examined and the applicant has also been granted bail in M.Cr.C.
No.51556 of 2024 dated 11.12.2024, and in this order also this Court has taken note of the condition imposed in the earlier order of bail of the respondent No.1, and thus, it is submitted that the application deserves to be rejected, as the daughter of the applicant has already solemnized marriage with the respondent No.1.
5] Counsel for the respondent No.2/State has submitted that appropriate orders may be passed.

6] Having considered the rival submissions, perusal of the documents filed on record, and taking note of the fact that the respondent No.1 has already been granted bail by this Court in the subsequent offence, wherein he had eloped with the same prosecutrix, who had earlier lodged the FIR against the respondent No.1, and he was granted bail by this Court in M.Cr.C. No.22788 of 2024 dated 12.07.2024.
In such circumstances, this Court does not find it to be a fit case to cancel the bail of the respondent No.1.
7] Accordingly, the application is hereby dismissed.

(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE Pankaj Dinesh vs Bhaarat @ Bharat Bawari on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105439962/
